questions.questionText: hour 15 minutes You must answer on the multiple choice answer sheet. You will need: Multiple choice answer sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) INSTRUCTIONS  There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
What is equivalent to social benefits?

options.A: the amount that the government spends on social security benefits
options.B: the benefit gained by society from total government spending
options.C: the benefit to third parties from household consumption of a good
options.D: the private and external benefits from household consumption of a good

Small farmers supply all their rice production to a single buyer. Which term best describes this market structure?

options.A: monopolistic
options.B: monopoly
options.C: monopsony
options.D: perfect competition

questions.questionText: A firm operating in an imperfectly competitive market decides to change its objective from sales revenue maximisation to sales volume maximisation. Why might it have decided to do this? increase short-run maximise short-run minimise short-run profits market share average costs

options.A: no no yes
options.B: no yes no
options.C: yes no yes
options.D: yes yes no

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the marginal cost (MC), average cost (AC), marginal revenue (MR) and average revenue (AR) curves of a profit-maximising, monopolistically competitive firm. cost and revenue MC AC AR O quantity MR Based on its profit, and assuming no market growth, what is likely to happen to the demand for this firm’s output in the long run?

options.A: The short-run profit position will encourage other firms to enter the market and the firm’s demand curve will shift to the left.
options.B: The short-run profit position will encourage other firms to enter the market and the firm’s demand curve will shift to the right.
options.C: The short-run profit position will encourage other firms to exit the market and the firm’s demand curve will shift to the left.
options.D: The short-run profit position will encourage other firms to exit the market and the firm’s demand curve will shift to the right.

questions.questionText: A monopoly firm is producing output OT, and selling its product at price OW, thereby maximising its profits, as shown. AC X W AC-subsidy price Y MC Z V AR O T quantity MR The government now decides that the firm’s operation generates positive externalities, and so gives the firm a subsidy. Assuming that the firm continues to seek maximum profit, what will result?

options.A: The firm continues to produce OT, and price remains at OW.
options.B: The firm continues to produce OT, but charges a lower price.
options.C: The firm increases production above OT, and reduces price.
options.D: The firm reduces production below OT, and reduces price by the amount of the subsidy.

questions.questionText: In many developed economies, large and small firms often exist side by side in the same industry. What is most likely to explain the survival of the small firms?

options.A: They each offer a much wider range of products.
options.B: They have a higher minimum efficient scale.
options.C: They pay much higher wages to their staff.
options.D: They provide a more personal level of consumer service.

questions.questionText: What is generally associated with the principal agent problem?

options.A: Directors prefer company growth to greater shareholder dividends.
options.B: Managers ignore workers’ concerns about safety in the workplace.
options.C: Shareholders determine the price of products.
options.D: Workers go on strike against managers’ reorganisation plans.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to reduce the negative externalities caused by the use of coal. Which policy should the government use?

options.A: Impose an indirect tax on the production of hydroelectric power.
options.B: Increase income tax.
options.C: Remove any restrictions on coal production.
options.D: Subsidise wind-powered electricity production.

questions.questionText: What would be an example of ‘nudge’ theory?

options.A: a subsidy on fresh fruit to increase demand
options.B: a unit tax on unhealthy food to reduce demand
options.C: banning all unhealthy food to reduce demand
options.D: putting fresh fruit at eye level in shops to increase demand

questions.questionText: When is a policy of income redistribution from rich people to poor people most appropriate?

options.A: when control of demand-pull inflation is the priority
options.B: when equality is valued more highly than efficiency
options.C: when monetary reward is the best incentive to risk-taking
options.D: when the rich have higher marginal utility curves than the poor

questions.questionText: Which diagram correctly shows the relationship between the average product (AP) and the marginal product (MP) of labour, given that the quantities of other factor inputs remain constant?

options.A: B average average MP AP product, product, marginal marginal product product AP MP O O labour labour
options.C: D MP average average AP product, product, marginal marginal product product MP AP O OO labour labour

questions.questionText: Wages in industry X are significantly higher than in industry Y. What could explain this difference?

options.A: Workers in industry Y are highly mobile.
options.B: Trade union organisation in industry Y is relatively strong.
options.C: Industries X and Y compete with each other for workers.
options.D: Industry Y has non-monetary advantages.

questions.questionText: Economic growth has both benefits and costs. In which situation would living standards be judged to have definitely increased?

options.A: As countries became industrialised, economic growth led to a fall in hours worked, as well as a rise in real incomes.
options.B: China had a huge rise in real GDP per head in the last 20 years but there was a decrease in air quality in urban areas.
options.C: Economic growth in high-income countries has seen childhood obesity increase, but has also seen increased resources devoted to its treatment.
options.D: The 1990s saw a significant rise in real GDP per head in the US with only a relatively small increase in the Gini coefficient during the same period.

questions.questionText: What is not included in National Income accounts?

options.A: a gift by a parent to her daughter as a deposit on an apartment
options.B: earnings of a part-time worker in a school dining room
options.C: interest earned on savings accounts intended for retirement
options.D: profits re-invested by a company to fund capital expenditure

questions.questionText: A government wishes to attract foreign direct investment to assist the development of its economy. What is most likely to encourage this?

options.A: improved health and safety standards for workers
options.B: increased import quotas
options.C: increased spending on infrastructure
options.D: introducing a minimum wage

questions.questionText: Which indicator is least likely to be used when measuring the comparative economic development of a country?

options.A: adult literacy rate
options.B: average life expectancy at birth
options.C: level of real GNP per head
options.D: size of population

questions.questionText: Which term is given to short-term unemployment when people are changing jobs?

options.A: cyclical
options.B: frictional
options.C: seasonal
options.D: voluntary

questions.questionText: The table shows data for an economy’s labour market. million number of people of working age 42.7 number of people of working age who are 2.2 actively seeking work, but are not working number of people of working age who are 9.4 not actively seeking work What is the economy’s percentage employment rate, to the nearest whole number?
Rapid economic growth is claimed by some to harm the environment. Which outcome would not harm the environment?

options.A: the greater mobility of workers resulting from increased vehicle ownership
options.B: the increased levels of income that reduce fertility rates and family size
options.C: the relocation of workers from agricultural to manufacturing employment
options.D: the use of improved technology to access previously inaccessible natural resources

Which statement would be associated with Keynesian economic theory?

options.A: A change in the money supply is the main determinant of the rate of inflation.
options.B: When unemployment falls below its natural rate, there is upward pressure on prices.
options.C: Total spending in the economy affects real output and employment in the short run.
options.D: Wages and prices are flexible so output and employment will always return to its equilibrium rate.

questions.questionText: In a closed economy with no government sector, the multiplier shows the impact of a change in

options.A: consumption on investment.
options.B: investment on national income.
options.C: national income on consumption.
options.D: national income on investment.

questions.questionText: In year 1, countries X and Y are each in balance of payments equilibrium. In year 2, country X, an exporter of oil, raises the price of its oil, which increases its foreign earnings by $500m, half of which is deposited with banks in country Y. Country Y is an important buyer of X’s oil and the price rise increases its foreign expenditure by $400m. Other things remaining equal, what are the total currency flows for X and Y? X ($m) Y ($m)
What does the Laffer curve show?

options.A: the relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment
options.B: the relationship between the rate of interest and the speculative demand for money
options.C: the relationship between tax rates and the amount of tax revenue collected by governments
options.D: the relationship between how two goods can be produced in an economy with given resources
